outcome.technical: DESIGN. run-test-gate.py: base_commands now asks _declared_suites_at_base(step, manifest, phase_id, tree) for a red step whose command the row keeps verbatim: a DECLARED step (step_parts == (name, [])) whose runner named failing suites, list not cut (_suites_cut), every suite a file of the base tree by its own normalized repo-relative path (_tree_suite), and whose name AND kept command are each the bare form of the plan's recorded spelling (_affected_tests.is_bare_entry) is spelled as _affected_tests.spelled_entry(named) and named _evidence_io.base_suites_step_name(name, named) (round-trip checked through base_suites_of), its command published so the base row keeps it verbatim for _same_call_over. Anything else runs whole as before. It measures EVERY suite the red names, not only the ones no kept base answers, so one run measured for the red answers the whole red and carries its recorder writes. Reading side: new _per_suite_base(step, head, task_id, rows, base_steps) -> {suite: (run, base step)} via _evidence_io.suite_base_run/suite_base_step, None when a whole-step base step answers the step by name or _evidence_io._suites_unmeasured is None (the same precondition base_unmeasured uses, so the two readers never disagree). _charge_step gains per_suite=None: a suite is answered only by its own per-suite base step; one none ran is not comparable. base_red takes base_row_for's run plus the per-suite runs; run = newest (_ev.oldest_first, after the ts-text lint fired on my first sort), and BASE_RUNS_READ_KEY='runs' lists them when more than one; basis names each. uncarried now asks every run the reading took (moves all introduced suites when any was measured for another red - conservative; the base measured for this red then answers all). kept_base_answer unchanged in code: it already reads base_unmeasured + base_reading, both now per-suite. EVICTION DECISION: kept bases stay keyed by commit and evicted by run id (MAX_KEPT_BASE_RUNS newest, _evidence_io.with_kept_bases unchanged). Reason: eviction can never make a base answer a suite it did not run (suite_base_step guards that), so its only cost is one re-measurement, which is now the red's suites rather than the whole step; keying by (commit, suite) would grow the plan record with the count of distinct suites against the size bound eviction exists for, and would change _evidence_io (not in this task's files). bps5 locks the choice (mutation MAX_KEPT_BASE_RUNS=3 in a throwaway copy -> bps5 red). TESTS (tests/test_run_test_gate.py, new staged blocks bps-block and bpr-block): bps1 one red suite -> runner call log exactly ['tests/test_t.py'], step 'selftests + affected/base: tests/test_t.py', base_commands command 'python3 tools/sweep.py tests/test_t.py', read introduced; bps2 two suites, one call, read case by case (same case at base -> atBase, other case -> introduced); bps3 runner named no suite -> whole step, calls [''] ; bps4 kept per-suite base answers the same red with nothing run (ledger gone), a red naming another suite runs that suite alone; bps5 third suite's base evicts the oldest: kept suite answered with nothing run, evicted suite re-measured alone; bps6 fallbacks (cut list, relative suite, missing suite -> whole; non-bare declared step as recorded; allow twin narrowed); bps7 two per-suite runs answer one red, a suite no step ran is not comparable; bps8 every run read is asked about the recorder's writes (older run uncarried -> moved), twin held=False charged. Fixture: fake sweep logging argv outside the tree; reds recorded with --no-reuse (an identical tree repeats a verdict with no head).
